checklist.name: chronic recurrent multifocal osteomyelitis

quotes.text: CRMO being the prominent phenotype in Majeed syndrome with 91 percent having radiologic or clinical evidence of CRMO
nearly all patients presented with chronic recurrent multifocal osteomyelitis (CRMO)

checklist.why: Defining feature of the triad and the most frequent finding (91% and 94.3% in the two patient reviews).

checklist.name: bone pain

quotes.text: The CRMO of Majeed syndrome presents with recurrent episodes of bone pain affecting the long bones
Each child presented in the first 2 years of life with recurrent fevers and bone pain

checklist.why: Presenting symptom, and the only bone finding in patients who were not imaged.

checklist.name: joint pain

quotes.text: Joint and bone pain
one adult had only mild knee pain throughout his childhood and adult life
recurrent swelling and pain of the knees and ankles

checklist.why: Recorded in mildly affected relatives and drives the frequent misdiagnosis as juvenile idiopathic arthritis.

checklist.name: joint or limb swelling

quotes.text: Recurrent fever and joint swelling were frequent manifestations
Objective limb swelling | 54

checklist.why: Objective musculoskeletal sign tabulated per patient in both patient reviews.

checklist.name: warmth or redness over bone or joint

quotes.text: objective changes on physical examination such as swelling or warmth overlying the involved bone or nearby joint
accompanied by limping and occasional redness

checklist.why: Local inflammatory sign that the first review names beside swelling as an examination finding.

checklist.name: joint contractures

quotes.text: sometimes with subsequent joint contractures due to severe multifocal sterile osteomyelitis

checklist.why: Complication of severe bone disease in the first families.

checklist.name: osteonecrosis

quotes.text: the seventh demonstrating osteonecrosis

checklist.why: Bone biopsy finding reported in place of osteomyelitis in one patient.

checklist.name: recurrent fever

quotes.text: Nearly half of the patients have recurrent fevers and for many this is one of the first manifestations of the disease
Recurrent fever | 23/30
Periodic fever may be present in some patients

checklist.why: Frequent early sign that places the disease among the periodic fever syndromes.

checklist.name: microcytic anemia

quotes.text: The anemia of Majeed syndrome is hypochromic and microcytic
Microcytic hypochromic anemia; elevated CRP and ESR

checklist.why: Blood finding of the second triad feature; severity varies widely and is stated per patient.

checklist.name: dyserythropoiesis on bone marrow

quotes.text: Bone marrow aspiration or biopsy demonstrates morphological abnormalities, such as erythroid hyperplasia with binuclearity or multinuclearity, which is typical of CDA
CDA present | 29/34

checklist.why: Marrow finding on which the CDA diagnosis rests; absent or not examined in some patients.

checklist.name: neutrophilic dermatosis (Sweet syndrome)

quotes.text: only 2 of 24 affected individuals had skin disease, both with the neutrophilic dermatosis Sweet syndrome
inflammatory cutaneous manifestations such as neutrophilic dermatosis or Sweet syndrome

checklist.why: Third feature of the classic triad; rare and possibly transient.

checklist.name: failure to thrive

quotes.text: significant failure to thrive and growth delay
Failure to thrive | 20/27

checklist.why: Tabulated per patient in both patient reviews.

checklist.name: growth delay

quotes.text: failure to thrive, growth delay and organomegaly that are present in ~ 30% of affected individuals
growth retardation and splenomegaly

checklist.why: Named apart from failure to thrive (weight) in both reviews.

checklist.name: hepatomegaly

quotes.text: often with hepatosplenomegaly
Hepatosplenomegaly | 30

checklist.why: Part of the organomegaly in about 30% of patients; split from splenomegaly because papers can state each organ separately.

checklist.name: splenomegaly

quotes.text: growth retardation and splenomegaly or a paravertebral mass
often with hepatosplenomegaly

checklist.why: Named on its own in the bone-disease review and as part of hepatosplenomegaly in the first review.

checklist.name: paravertebral mass

quotes.text: a paravertebral mass secondary to congenital dyserythropoietic anemia may be observed

checklist.why: Complication of the anemia that a case report would state as present or absent on imaging.

checklist.name: neonatal jaundice

quotes.text: These patients may also experience neonatal jaundice and neutropenia

checklist.why: Early hematologic sign named for Majeed syndrome in the bone-disease review.

checklist.name: elevated inflammatory markers (ESR/CRP)

quotes.text: Elevated blood inflammatory markers were present in 21 of 21 patients tested
Laboratory findings consistently demonstrated anemia, elevated ESR and CRP

checklist.why: Present in nearly every patient tested; usually reported with values.

checklist.name: elevated proinflammatory cytokines

quotes.text: proinflammatory cytokines such as IL-1β, IL-6, IL-8, and TNF-α are known to be increased in patients with Majeed syndrome
Pro-inflammatory cytokines were markedly increased

checklist.why: Serum cytokine levels (IL-6, TNF and others) are increasingly measured and reported in case reports.

checklist.name: neutropenia

quotes.text: Neutropenia | 13
neonatal jaundice and neutropenia

checklist.why: Laboratory finding tabulated per patient with absolute counts.

left_out: red blood cell transfusion requirement: a treatment, and narrower than microcytic anemia
sites of bone involvement (lower-limb and upper-limb long bones, feet, hands, ribs, spine): each sits inside chronic recurrent multifocal osteomyelitis
bone marrow edema or osteolytic lesions with sclerosis on imaging (41113563, Table 3): imaging evidence of chronic recurrent multifocal osteomyelitis, so it would sit inside that item
culture-negative, neutrophilic or granulomatous osteomyelitis on biopsy: sits inside chronic recurrent multifocal osteomyelitis
elevated platelets: 41113563 Table 2 counts platelets among the inflammatory markers and gives no separate figure
leukopenia: one table cell ('leuko') in 33670882; overlaps neutropenia
dimorphic red cells, hypochromia, anisocytosis, erythroid hyperplasia: details of the anemia and dyserythropoiesis items
limping, elevated fibrinogen, pneumatosis, enhanced lung markings: reported only in the single 41113563 case, not described as features of the disease
tremor, ataxia and other neurologic signs: reported only in Lpin2-deficient mice; 33670882 says they have 'not been reported in Majeed syndrome'
lipid abnormalities: 33670882 says 'No abnormalities in fat metabolism have been identified in Majeed syndrome'
inflammatory bowel disease, psoriasis, inflammatory arthritis, pustulosis, clavicle and vertebral lesions: described for non-syndromic CRMO, SAPHO or DIRA, not Majeed syndrome
raised caspase-1 activity and osteoclastogenesis in patient cells: in vitro research findings, not case-report features
notes: Three sources were used because the first review (Ferguson 2021, PMID 33670882) supports only about 15 distinct, non-overlapping features; the coordinator approved adding Wang 2025 (PMID 41113563, case report plus a review of 35 patients) and Haşlak 2025 (PMID 39757386, review of autoinflammatory bone diseases, Majeed section only). Features resting on one source: neonatal jaundice and paravertebral mass (39757386, one sentence each, citing primary reports); joint contractures and osteonecrosis (33670882, one sentence each; osteonecrosis is one patient's biopsy). Hepatomegaly and splenomegaly are split because 39757386 names splenomegaly alone while 33670882 names hepatosplenomegaly. 'Dyserythropoiesis on bone marrow' is kept apart from 'microcytic anemia' (marrow vs blood finding); papers that say only 'CDA' without marrow findings will need a stated rule. Elevated inflammatory markers are ESR/CRP; cytokines are a separate item. All quotes were checked verbatim against the three Markdown files.
